summary: ltrim removes characters only from the beginning of text.
documentation: ltrim removes characters only from the beginning of text. Its second argument is a set of removable characters, not one exact prefix. Without it, SQLite removes ordinary leading spaces.
inputs: Text and an optional character set.
returns: Text with matching leading characters removed, or NULL.
caution: All consecutive leading characters from the set are removed in any order. Trailing and interior matches remain unchanged.
scenarios: Remove a known leading padding convention from imported codes.
Strip several allowed separator characters from a report label.
Clean leading spaces while preserving right-hand formatting.
title: Remove leading padding characters
problem: From codes(id INTEGER, code TEXT), return id and ltrim(code, '0-') as cleaned, ordered by id. Remove any run of leading zeroes and hyphens; keep all trailing or interior zeroes and hyphens. NULL remains NULL.
goal: Use ltrim() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Treat 0- as a character set, not an exact two-character prefix.
